Multiple risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD), but without established CHD.

Adults with primary hyperlipidemia.
Adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).
As an adjunct to other LDL-lowering therapies:
For adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

For adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

As a result, it lowers overall LDL levels.
It decreases the number of LDL particles.
It improves the body's ability to clear cholesterol.

graph_edge.subject: Lipitor
graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug is typically prescribed at the dose or dosing regimen specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Recommended Dosage in Adult Patients The recommended starting dosage of Lipitor is 10 mg to 20 mg once daily.
The dosage range is 10 mg to 80 mg once daily.
Patients who require a reduction in LDL-C greater than 45% may be started at 40 mg once daily.
Recommended Dosage in Pediatric Patients 10 Years of Age and Older with HeFH The recommended starting dosage of Lipitor is 10 mg once daily.
The dosage range is 10 mg to 20 mg once daily.
Recommended Dosage in Pediatric Patients 10 Years of Age and Older with HoFH The recommended starting dosage of Lipitor is 10 mg to 20 mg once daily.
The dosage range is 10 mg to 80 mg once daily.
Assess LDL-C when clinically appropriate.
Do this as early as 4 weeks after initiating Lipitor.
Adjust the dosage if necessary.
This medicine is available as: atorvastatin 10 mg tablets, atorvastatin 20 mg tablets, atorvastatin 40 mg tablet, 80 mg tablets.
The original brand name of atorvastatin was Lipitor.
Now it is also available as a generic.
Atorvastatin calcium oral suspension is also available as the brand Aorvaliq 20mg/5ml.

graph_edge.subject: Atorvastatin
graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medicines at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you use.
This can increase the risk of serious muscle problems.
This can make the medicines less effective.
Tell your doctor about all your current medicines.
Many drugs can interact with atorvastatin, especially:
other cholesterol-lowering medicines - gemfibrozil, niacin, fenofibrate, fenofibric acid, and others;
colchicine;
antibiotic or antifungal medicine - rifampin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, and voriconazole;
birth control pills;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection; or
antiviral medicine to treat hepatitis C, HIV, or cytomegalovirus (such as letermovir).
This list is not complete.
Many other drugs may interact with atorvastatin.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.

Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medicines at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you use.
This can increase the risk of serious muscle problems.
This can make the medicines less effective.
Tell your doctor about all your current medicines.

other cholesterol-lowering medicines - gemfibrozil, niacin, fenofibrate, fenofibric acid, and others;
colchicine;
antibiotic or antifungal medicine - rifampin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, and voriconazole;
birth control pills;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection; or
antiviral medicine to treat hepatitis C, HIV, or cytomegalovirus (such as letermovir).
This list is not complete.
Many other drugs may interact with atorvastatin.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
You should not take atorvastatin if you have liver disease or cirrhosis.
Atorvastatin can cause the breakdown of muscle tissue.
The breakdown of muscle tissue can lead to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
Do so especially if you also have fever, unusual tiredness, or dark urine.
Serious drug interactions can occur when certain medicines are used together with atorvastatin.
Tell each of your healthcare providers about all medicines you use now, and any medicine you start or stop using.
Avoid eating foods that are high in fat or cholesterol.
Atorvastatin will not be as effective in lowering your cholesterol.
This is because you do not follow a cholesterol-lowering diet plan.
Atorvastatin is only part of a complete program of treatment that also includes diet, exercise, and weight control.
Follow your diet, medication, and exercise routines very closely.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Levothyroxine is a man-made form of thyroxine (T4), one of the hormones your thyroid gland normally produces.
It belongs to a class of medications called hormones.
It works by replacing thyroid hormone that your body is not making enough of.
Levothyroxine is used in adults and children, including newborn babies, to:
treat hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid - a condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormone).
It replaces the missing hormone whether the condition was present from birth or developed later.
It replaces the missing hormone whether the problem starts in the thyroid gland itself or in the pituitary gland or hypothalamus.
lower the level of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood in people being treated for a certain type of thyroid cancer, alongside surgery and radioactive iodine therapy.
Levothyroxine injection is used in adults to treat myxedema coma.
Myxedema coma is a rare and life-threatening complication.
Myxedema coma is a complication of a severely underactive thyroid.
Without thyroid hormone, your body cannot function properly.

Without thyroid hormone, your body cannot function properly.

Your doctor will aim to give you the lowest dose that controls your thyroid levels.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Metformin is prescribed to manage polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
It is prescribed because it improves how the body responds to insulin.
PCOS affects about 1 in 10 women of reproductive age.
PCOS is often marked by insulin resistance.
Insulin resistance is a condition in which the body doesn't respond well to insulin.
Poor response to insulin prompts the pancreas to produce more.
This excess insulin drives up androgen production.
Androgen is a male hormone.
This process worsens symptoms like irregular periods, infertility, acne, and excess hair growth.
Metformin helps by lowering insulin levels.
Metformin helps by decreasing the liver's glucose production.
Metformin helps by improving glucose uptake by muscles.
Metformin helps by reducing circulating androgen levels.
Reducing circulating androgen levels can support more regular ovulation.
Reducing circulating androgen levels can support more regular menstrual cycles.
Metformin is not FDA-approved to treat PCOS.
Metformin is widely prescribed as an off-label treatment.

Mitochondrial diseases are certain rare inherited metabolic disorders.
Stop taking metformin and call your healthcare professional immediately if you have any symptoms of lactic acidosis, including if you feel:
very weak and tired
have unusual (not normal) muscle pain
have trouble breathing
have unusual sleepiness or sleep longer than usual
have unexplained stomach or intestinal problems with nausea and vomiting, or diarrhea
cold, especially in your arms and legs
dizzy or lightheaded
have a slow or irregular heartbeat
Other warnings:
Vitamin B12 deficiency: Metformin can lower your vitamin B12 levels over time.
Your doctor may check your blood counts every year.
Your doctor may check your B12 levels every 2 to 3 years.
This is done to catch any problems early.
Low blood sugar is a risk when taken with insulin or other diabetes medicines.
Taking metformin along with insulin or certain other diabetes drugs raises the risk of low blood sugar.
These certain other diabetes drugs are ones that boost insulin release.
If you're on one of these combinations.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Does metformin work for weight loss?
:
Yes.
Metformin can lead to a modest weight loss.
Results vary.
The weight loss from Metformin is generally smaller than what is seen with medications specifically approved for weight loss.
In the landmark Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP), participants taking metformin lost more weight than those on placebo.
The DPP was a randomized controlled trial in people at high risk for diabetes.
Metformin patients lost 2.7% of body weight after one year.
This was compared to 0.43% for placebo.
Metformin patients also lost 2.1% of body weight after two years.
This was compared to essentially no change (0.02%) for placebo.
29% of people on metformin lost at least 5% of their starting body weight after one year.
Just 13% of people on placebo lost at least 5% of their starting body weight after one year.
This gap held up at the two-year mark.
At the two-year mark, 26% of people on metformin lost at least 5% of their starting body weight.
At the two-year mark, 14% of people on placebo lost at least 5% of their starting body weight.

graph_edge.evidence_text:
Amlodipine besylate is a prescription medicine.
It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
It belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, this medicine controls chest pain.
It does not stop chest pain once it starts.
Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take when you have chest pain.
Amlodipine is also used alone or in combination with other medicines to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.
Amlodipine besylate is available as:
Amlodipine 5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 1 mg/mL solution (Norliqva)

The initial dose is 5 mg orally within 24 hours of the onset of acute myocardial infarction.

Therapy should be initiated at 2.5 mg.

Therapy should be initiated during the first 3 days after the infarct.
Therapy should be withdrawn.
This occurs if prolonged hypotension happens.

Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

It could harm the unborn baby.
Stop using this medicine and tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant.
You should not use this medicine if you have ever had angioedema.

Blood flows more smoothly.
The heart can pump blood more efficiently.
High blood pressure is a common condition.

It may cause heart failure.
It may cause a stroke.
It may cause kidney failure.
It may cause loss of vision.
It may cause other problems.
Taking medication will help to control your blood pressure.
Making lifestyle changes will also help to control your blood pressure.
These changes include eating a diet that is low in fat and salt.

graph_edge.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril.
Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

insulin or diabetes medications;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection such as temsirolimus, sirolimus, or everolimus; or
heart or blood pressure medication
lithium
gold injections.

If you have high blood pressure, keep using lisinopril even if you feel well.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms.
Store tightly closed at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
Do not freeze.

candidate_edges.subject: Lisinopril
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug may be used for the medical purpose or indication specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Usual Adult Dose for Hypertension:
The initial dose is 10 mg orally once a day.
The maintenance dose is 20 to 40 mg orally once a day.
The maximum dose is 80 mg orally once a day.
The initial dose is 5 mg orally once a day in patients receiving a diuretic.
-The 80 mg dose is used but does not appear to give greater effect.
If blood pressure is not controlled with lisinopril alone, a low dose of a diuretic may be added.
Hydrochlorothiazide is an example of such a diuretic.
The dose of hydrochlorothiazide is 12.5 mg.
It may be possible to reduce the dose of lisinopril.
This is after the addition of a diuretic.
Usual Adult Dose for Congestive Heart Failure:
Initial dose: 2.5 to 5 mg orally once a day.
Maintenance dose: Dosage should be increased as tolerated.
Maximum dose: 40 mg orally once a day.
The diuretic dose may need to be adjusted.
This adjustment may help minimize hypovolemia.
Hypovolemia may contribute to hypotension.
The appearance of hypotension after the initial dose of lisinopril does not preclude subsequent careful dose titration.
The drug is used for this titration.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril.
Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Usual Geriatric Dose for Hypertension:
Initial dose: 2.5 to 5 mg orally once a day.
Maintenance dose: Dosages should be increased at 2.5 mg to 5 mg per day at 1 to 2 week intervals.
Maximum dose: 40 mg orally once a day
Usual Pediatric Dose for Hypertension:
Pediatric patients greater than or equal to 6 years of age were studied.
The initial dose was 0.07 mg/kg orally once a day.
The maximum initial dose is 5 mg once a day.
The maintenance dose should be adjusted according to blood pressure response.
Adjustments should occur at 1 to 2 week intervals.
Maximum dose: Doses above 0.61 mg/kg or greater than 40 mg have not been studied in pediatric patients.
This drug is not recommended in pediatric patients less than 6 years old.
This drug is not recommended in pediatric patients with glomerular filtration rate less than 30 mL/min.

candidate_edges.subject: Lisinopril
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug may be used for the medical purpose or indication specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:

The initial dose is 10 mg orally once a day.
The maintenance dose is 20 to 40 mg orally once a day.
The maximum dose is 80 mg orally once a day.
The initial dose is 5 mg orally once a day in patients receiving a diuretic.
-The 80 mg dose is used but does not appear to give greater effect.
If blood pressure is not controlled with lisinopril alone, a low dose of a diuretic may be added.
Hydrochlorothiazide is an example of such a diuretic.
The dose of hydrochlorothiazide is 12.5 mg.
It may be possible to reduce the dose of lisinopril.
This is after the addition of a diuretic.
Usual Adult Dose for Congestive Heart Failure:
Initial dose: 2.5 to 5 mg orally once a day.
Maintenance dose: Dosage should be increased as tolerated.
Maximum dose: 40 mg orally once a day.
The diuretic dose may need to be adjusted.
This adjustment may help minimize hypovolemia.
Hypovolemia may contribute to hypotension.
The appearance of hypotension after the initial dose of lisinopril does not preclude subsequent careful dose titration.
The drug is used for this titration.

candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
It is important to keep albuterol on hand at all times.
Get your prescription refilled before you run out of medicine completely.
Keep using all of your other medications as prescribed by your doctor.
Talk with your doctor if any of your asthma medications do not seem to work as well in treating or preventing attacks.
If it seems like you need to use more of any of your medications in a 24-hour period, talk with your doctor.
An increased need for medication could be an early sign of a serious asthma attack.
Only use albuterol as prescribed by your physician.
An overdose of albuterol can be fatal.
Seek emergency medical attention or call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222.

candidate_edges.subject: Albuterol Inhalation
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
You should not use this medicine if you are allergic to albuterol.
You should not use ProAir RespiClick or ProAir Digihaler if you are allergic to milk proteins.
To make sure albuterol inhalation is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have:
heart disease, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure;
a heart rhythm disorder;
a seizure disorder such as epilepsy;
diabetes;
overactive thyroid; or
low levels of potassium in your blood.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
It is not known whether albuterol will harm an unborn baby.
However, having uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy may increase the risk of premature birth.
It may also increase the risk of low birth weight.
It may also increase the risk of eclampsia.
Eclampsia is dangerously high blood pressure.
Eclampsia can lead to medical problems in both mother and baby.
The benefit of preventing bronchospasm may outweigh any risks to the baby.
If you are pregnant, your name may be listed on a pregnancy registry.
The registry is used to track the effects of albuterol on the baby.

candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to losartan.
These signs include hives, difficulty breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Losartan may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement; or
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath.
Common losartan side effects may include:
dizziness, tiredness;
low blood pressure;
low blood sugar;
diarrhea;
back pain; or
cold symptoms such as stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to metoprolol.
These signs include hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Common side effects of metoprolol:
In studies of people taking metoprolol for high blood pressure or angina:
Tiredness and dizziness occurred in about 10% of people
Low mood or depression was reported in about 5 out of 100 people
Diarrhea occurred in about 5% of people
Itching or rash occurred in about 5% of people
Shortness of breath and a slow heartbeat occurred in about 3% of people
Cold hands and feet, palpitations, swelling of the ankles, and low blood pressure were each reported in about 1% of people
Nausea, dry mouth, stomach pain, constipation, gas, and heartburn were each reported in about 1% of people

The most common side effects of metoprolol are tiredness, dizziness, low mood (depression), diarrhea, shortness of breath, a slow heartbeat (bradycardia), and itching or rash.
Most side effects reported in studies were mild and did not last.
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to metoprolol.
These signs include hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Common side effects of metoprolol:
In studies of people taking metoprolol for high blood pressure or angina:
Tiredness and dizziness occurred in about 10% of people
Low mood or depression was reported in about 5 out of 100 people
Diarrhea occurred in about 5% of people
Itching or rash occurred in about 5% of people
Shortness of breath and a slow heartbeat occurred in about 3% of people
Cold hands and feet, palpitations, swelling of the ankles, and low blood pressure were each reported in about 1% of people
Nausea, dry mouth, stomach pain, constipation, gas, and heartburn were each reported in about 1% of people

graph_edge.evidence_text:
Metoprolol is a beta-blocker medication.
Metoprolol is used to treat high blood pressure.
Metoprolol is used to treat chest pain (angina).
Metoprolol is used to treat heart failure.
Metoprolol is used to improve survival after a heart attack.
It works mainly on the heart.
It is called a cardioselective beta-blocker.
Metoprolol works by blocking the effect of adrenaline and noradrenaline on beta-1 receptors in your heart.
This slows your heart rate.
It reduces how hard your heart squeezes.
It lowers your blood pressure.
The heart is doing less work.
Because the heart is doing less work, it needs less oxygen.
Metoprolol helps with angina.
Metoprolol helps with angina because the heart needs less oxygen.
Exactly how metoprolol works is not fully understood.
Metoprolol is used for high blood pressure, heart failure, and after a heart attack.
At higher blood levels, metoprolol also blocks beta-2 receptors in the airways and blood vessels.
This is why it still needs care in people with breathing problems.

The two forms are not approved for the same conditions.
Condition | Metoprolol tartrate (immediate release) | Metoprolol succinate (extended release)
High blood pressure (hypertension) in adults | Yes | Yes
High blood pressure in children 6 years and older | No | Yes
Angina (chest pain) | Yes | Yes
Heart failure | No | Yes
Heart attack (myocardial infarction) | Yes | No
High blood pressure (hypertension).
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal heart and blood vessel events.
These events mainly include strokes and heart attacks.
Metoprolol can be used on its own or with other blood pressure medicines.
Many people need more than one medicine to reach their blood pressure goal.
Angina.
Metoprolol is used for long-term treatment of angina.
It is used to reduce how often attacks happen.
It is used to help you do more before chest pain starts.
It is not used to stop an attack that has already begun.
Heart failure.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
The interactions that matter most are medicines that also slow the heart.
The interactions that matter most are medicines that block the liver enzyme CYP2D6.
This enzyme raises metoprolol levels in your blood.
Digoxin, clonidine, diltiazem, and verapamil.
These all slow the heart's electrical signal and heart rate.
Taking them with metoprolol raises the risk of a very slow heartbeat.
Clonidine, when stopping either medicine.
You take both medications.
Metoprolol is stopped several days before clonidine is withdrawn.
Clonidine is withdrawn slowly.
Beta blockers can worsen blood pressure rebound.
Blood pressure rebound follows clonidine withdrawal.
Quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, and propafenone.
These strong CYP2D6 blockers double the amount of metoprolol in your blood.
Quinidine tripled levels of one form of metoprolol and doubled how long it lasted.
Weaker CYP2D6 blockers are likely to raise levels too.
Reserpine and MAO inhibitors.
These deplete adrenaline-type chemicals.
These can add to metoprolol's effect.
This can cause low blood pressure or a marked slowing of the heart.

graph_edge.evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

Rosuvastatin may cause serious side effects, including:

Tell your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
Tell your doctor right away if you have a fever.
Tell your doctor right away if you feel more tired than usual.
These symptoms may occur while you take this medicine.
you have muscle problems that do not go away even after your doctor has told you to stop taking this medicine.

LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.

Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

erosive esophagitis (EE) caused by acid reflux in adults and children 1 month of age and older

graph_edge.evidence_text:
Taking omeprazole long-term may cause you to develop stomach growths called fundic gland polyps.
Talk with your doctor about this risk.
If you use this medicine for longer than 3 years, you could develop a vitamin B-12 deficiency.
Talk to your doctor if you develop symptoms.
These symptoms include shortness of breath, lightheadedness, irregular heartbeat, muscle weakness, pale skin, feeling tired, mood changes, and tingling or numbness in the arms and legs.
Common side effects of omeprazole may include:
cold symptoms such as stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat (especially in children);
fever (especially in children);
stomach pain, gas;
nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; or
headache.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

candidate_edges.subject: omeprazole
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Omeprazole can cause kidney problems.
Tell your doctor if you are urinating less than usual, or if you have blood in your urine.
Diarrhea may be a sign of a new infection.
Call your doctor right away if you have watery stools or stomach pain that does not go away.
You may or may not have a fever.
Omeprazole is not to be used for the immediate relief of heartburn symptoms.
Omeprazole may cause new or worsening symptoms of lupus.
Tell your doctor if you have joint pain and a skin rash on your cheeks or arms that worsens in sunlight.
You may be more likely to have a broken bone while taking this medicine long term or more than once per day.

Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.

This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.

Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.

Day 1: 300 mg orally with the evening meal
Day 2: 600 mg orally with the evening meal
Days 3 through 6: 900 mg orally with the evening meal
Days 7 through 10: 1200 mg orally with the evening meal
Days 11 through 14: 1500 mg orally with the evening meal
Day 15: 1800 mg orally with the evening meal
Notes
Gralise is not interchangeable with other gabapentin products.

graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug produces its therapeutic effect through the biological mechanism specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.
It isn't useful for everyday pain.
Everyday pain includes headaches.
Everyday pain includes sprains.

Major depressive disorder (MDD), the clinical term for depression.
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), where unwanted thoughts drive repeated behaviors.
Panic disorder, which causes sudden attacks of intense fear along with physical symptoms.
Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), which can follow a frightening or traumatic event.
Social anxiety disorder (SAD), also called social phobia.
Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a severe form of premenstrual symptoms.
In children and teenagers, sertraline is approved only for OCD, from age 6 upward.
Its safety and effectiveness have not been established in children under 6 years of age.
Its safety and effectiveness have not been established in children and teenagers for any condition other than OCD.
Not every sertraline product is approved for all six conditions:
Sertraline tablets and oral solution are approved for all of them.
Sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules are approved only for depression in adults and for OCD in adults and children aged 6 and over.

- Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), where unwanted thoughts drive repeated behaviors.
- Panic disorder, which causes sudden attacks of intense fear along with physical symptoms.
- Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), which can follow a frightening or traumatic event.
- Social anxiety disorder (SAD), also called social phobia.
- Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a severe form of premenstrual symptoms.

It is sold under the brand name Zoloft.
Generic sertraline is widely available.
Sertraline belongs to a group of medicines called selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs.
It increases serotonin activity in the brain.

How long does sertraline take to work?
:
Sertraline levels in the blood become steady after about a week of once daily dosing.
The effect on symptoms takes longer.
The trials that established sertraline ran for 6 to 12 weeks.
These trials were for depression.
These trials were for OCD.
These trials were for panic disorder.
These trials were for PTSD.
These trials were for social anxiety disorder.
The trials ran for over three menstrual cycles.
These trials were for PMDD.
This duration gives a sense of the time frame over which the benefit was measured.
It takes time.
Doses are usually raised no more often than once a week.
You should keep taking sertraline even if you do not feel a change yet.
How long does sertraline stay in your system?
:
Sertraline has a half-life of about 26 hours.
This means half of what is in your blood is cleared in roughly a day.
At that rate, most of a dose has left your bloodstream within about 5 to 6 days.
Its main breakdown product, N-desmethylsertraline, lasts longer.
It has a half-life of 62 to 104 hours.
It is much less active than sertraline itself.

Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), which can follow a frightening or traumatic event.
Social anxiety disorder (SAD), also called social phobia.
Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a severe form of premenstrual symptoms.
In children and teenagers, sertraline is approved only for OCD, from age 6 upward.

Sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules are approved only for depression in adults and for OCD in adults and children aged 6 and over.

Breastfeeding:
Low levels of sertraline and its breakdown products pass into breast milk.
A pooled analysis of 53 mother and infant pairs was conducted.
Exclusively breastfed infants had an average of 2% of the sertraline levels measured in their mothers' blood.
The levels ranged from 0% to 15%.
No side effects were seen in those infants.
There is no information on whether sertraline affects milk production.
Talk with your doctor about the benefits of breastfeeding alongside your need for treatment.
Children:
Sertraline is approved for OCD in children aged 6 to 17 years.

It is not known to be safe and effective for any other condition in this age group.
Children and teenagers taking sertraline should be monitored for worsening symptoms and suicidal thoughts.
This monitoring is especially important early in treatment and when the dose changes.
Their weight and growth should be checked.
Older adults:
Older adults clear sertraline more slowly.

Insomnia and agitation were more common in OCD trials.
Constipation and agitation were more common in panic disorder trials.

In PMDD trials, sleepiness, dry mouth, dizziness, tiredness, and stomach pain were more common.
In these trials, 12% of people taking sertraline stopped treatment.
They stopped treatment because of a side effect.
This was compared with 4% of people taking placebo.
The most common reason for stopping was nausea (3%).
Diarrhea (2%) was another common reason for stopping.
Agitation (2%) was also a common reason for stopping.
Insomnia (2%) was a common reason for stopping.

SSRIs including sertraline can cause sexual problems.
In men, this can mean delayed ejaculation or being unable to ejaculate.
In men, this can also mean lower sex drive.

Major depressive disorder (MDD), the clinical term for depression.
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), where unwanted thoughts drive repeated behaviors.
Panic disorder, which causes sudden attacks of intense fear along with physical symptoms.
Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), which can follow a frightening or traumatic event.
Social anxiety disorder (SAD), also called social phobia.
Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a severe form of premenstrual symptoms.
In children and teenagers, sertraline is approved only for OCD, from age 6 upward.
Its safety and effectiveness have not been established in children under 6 years of age.
Its safety and effectiveness have not been established in children and teenagers for any condition other than OCD.

Sertraline tablets and oral solution are approved for all of them.
Sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules are approved only for depression in adults and for OCD in adults and children aged 6 and over.

It is much less active than sertraline itself.

:
Sertraline levels in the blood become steady after about a week of once daily dosing.
The effect on symptoms takes longer.
The trials that established sertraline ran for 6 to 12 weeks.
These trials were for depression.
These trials were for OCD.
These trials were for panic disorder.
These trials were for PTSD.
These trials were for social anxiety disorder.
The trials ran for over three menstrual cycles.
These trials were for PMDD.
This duration gives a sense of the time frame over which the benefit was measured.
It takes time.
Doses are usually raised no more often than once a week.
You should keep taking sertraline even if you do not feel a change yet.
How long does sertraline stay in your system?
:
Sertraline has a half-life of about 26 hours.
This means half of what is in your blood is cleared in roughly a day.
At that rate, most of a dose has left your bloodstream within about 5 to 6 days.
Its main breakdown product, N-desmethylsertraline, lasts longer.
It has a half-life of 62 to 104 hours.
It is much less active than sertraline itself.

This risk applies to someone with bipolar disorder.

candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug is sold under or known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Is sertraline the same as Zoloft?
:
Yes.
Sertraline is the active ingredient.
Zoloft is the brand name it is sold under in the United States.
Sertraline is the generic version of Zoloft.
The two contain the same medicine, sertraline hydrochloride.
You may also see it written as sertraline HCl.
Is sertraline an SSRI, and how does it work?
:
Yes, sertraline is an SSRI, which stands for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.
Nerve cells in the brain release serotonin to send signals.
Then, they reabsorb it.
Sertraline blocks that reabsorption.
More serotonin stays available between nerve cells.
Sertraline has very little effect on norepinephrine.
Sertraline has very little effect on dopamine.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on adrenergic receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on cholinergic receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on GABA receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on histamine receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on benzodiazepine receptors.
This lack of effect on multiple receptors is part of why sertraline is described as selective.

candidate_edges.subject: sertraline
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug was evaluated in the clinical trial specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
In children and teenagers taking sertraline for depression, there was a difference in weight change of roughly 1 kg compared with placebo over 10 weeks.
This difference represented slight weight loss on sertraline.
This difference represented slight weight gain on placebo.
Around 7% of children lost more than 7% of their body weight, compared with none on placebo.
In a longer 34 week extension study, weight gain was similar to what would be expected for their age.
Height and weight should be monitored in younger patients.
Tell your doctor about any weight change that concerns you.
Does sertraline make you tired or sleepy?
:
It can.
Sleepiness was reported by 11% of adults taking sertraline in trials.
This was compared with 6% on placebo.
Tiredness was reported by 12%.
This was compared with 8%.
Sertraline can also affect how clearly you think and how quickly you react.
Do not drive or use machinery until you know how it affects you.
Is sertraline a controlled substance?
:
No.
Sertraline is not a controlled substance.
A study compared sertraline with alprazolam and d-amphetamine.

graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Several medicines interact with sertraline.
Give a full list of everything you take to any provider who treats you.
The most important interactions are:
MAOIs.
Taking sertraline with an MAOI raises the risk of serotonin syndrome.
The combination is contraindicated.
Examples include selegiline, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid, phenelzine, linezolid, and methylene blue.
Pimozide.
Sertraline raises pimozide levels.
This can lead to QTc prolongation.
This can lead to irregular heartbeats.
The combination is contraindicated.

Is sertraline an SSRI, and how does it work?
:
Yes, sertraline is an SSRI, which stands for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.
Nerve cells in the brain release serotonin to send signals.
Then, they reabsorb it.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
The oral solution specifically is not recommended in pregnancy because it contains alcohol.
What are sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules for?
:
Sertraline capsules come in 150 mg and 200 mg only.
They are not used to start treatment.
They are for people who have already been taking 100 mg or 125 mg of another sertraline product for at least a week and need a higher dose.
The maximum is 200 mg a day, the same as for tablets.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not opened, crushed, or chewed.
If you need to come off sertraline, the dose has to be lowered gradually.
This must be done using another sertraline product.
There is no capsule strength below 150 mg.
Capsules are approved for depression in adults.
Capsules are approved for OCD from age 6.
Capsules are not approved for panic disorder.
Capsules are not approved for PTSD.
Capsules are not approved for social anxiety disorder.
Capsules are not approved for PMDD.
Does sertraline interact with warfarin?
:
Yes, in two ways.
Sertraline can add to warfarin's effect on bleeding risk.

The maintenance dose is 10 to 20 mg orally once a day.
The maximum dose is 20 mg orally once a day.

-Patients should be periodically reassessed to determine the need for maintenance treatment.
Use: Acute and maintenance treatment of major depressive disorder

Take escitalopram exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Take escitalopram at the same time each day, with or without food.
Measure liquid medicine carefully.
Use the dosing syringe provided, or use a medicine dose-measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
It may take up to 4 weeks before your symptoms improve.
Keep using the medication as directed.
Tell your doctor if your symptoms do not improve.

Some sexual problems can be treated.
Your doctor will need to check your progress on a regular basis.
A child taking escitalopram should be checked for height and weight gain.
Do not stop using escitalopram suddenly.
You could have unpleasant withdrawal symptoms.
Follow your doctor's instructions about tapering your dose.

candidate_edges.subject: Semaglutide
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
You should not use semaglutide if you are allergic to it, or if you have:
multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (tumors in your glands);
a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (a type of thyroid cancer); or
diabetic ketoacidosis (call your doctor for treatment).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
a stomach or intestinal disorder;
pancreatitis;
are planning surgery or other procedure that uses anesthesia or deep sedation;
kidney disease; or
eye problems caused by diabetes (retinopathy).
In animal studies, semaglutide caused thyroid tumors or thyroid cancer.
It is not known whether these effects would occur in people.
Ask your doctor about your risk.
Pregnancy:
Men and women should stop using semaglutide at least 2 months before they plan to get pregnant.
Ask your doctor for a safer medicine to use during this time.
Controlling diabetes is very important during pregnancy.
Gaining the right amount of weight is also very important during pregnancy.
Even if you are overweight, losing weight during pregnancy could harm the unborn baby.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

In people with kidney disease, levels in the blood are higher.
In people with kidney disease, the medicine stays in the body longer.

This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

low potassium or low sodium levels
lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus)
glaucoma

candidate_edges.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug leads to or results in the effect or condition specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

candidate_edges.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are unable to pass urine (anuria).
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are allergic to hydrochlorothiazide or to other sulfonamide-derived medicines (sometimes called sulfa drugs).
Before you start HCTZ, tell your doctor if you have or have ever had:
kidney disease or reduced kidney function
liver disease, including cirrhosis
diabetes
gout or high uric acid levels
high cholesterol or high triglycerides
high calcium levels or a parathyroid gland disorder
low potassium or low sodium levels
lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus)
glaucoma
an allergy to sulfa medicines or to penicillin
Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
Hydrochlorothiazide may cause jaundice or bleeding problems in a newborn.
The medicine can pass into breast milk.
The medicine may cause serious side effects in a nursing baby.
You and your doctor should decide whether you will take this medicine.
You and your doctor should decide whether you will breastfeed.

weakness

muscle spasm
increased sensitivity to sunlight, causing sunburn more easily
hair loss or thinning
difficulty getting or keeping an erection
temporary blurred vision, or objects looking yellow-tinged (xanthopsia)
swelling and tenderness of the salivary glands

kidney disease or reduced kidney function
liver disease, including cirrhosis
diabetes
gout or high uric acid levels

low potassium or low sodium levels
lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus)
glaucoma

Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

candidate_edges.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

candidate_edges.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.

It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

Like all medications, Prozac carries some important warnings you should be aware of before and during treatment.
Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following.
Boxed warning:
Fluoxetine carries a boxed warning, the FDA's most serious warning, regarding suicidal thoughts and behavior.
Antidepressants may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts in children, adolescents, and young adults.
Fluoxetine is an antidepressant.
The risk is particularly high in the first few months of treatment.
The risk is also high when the dose is changed.
This risk was not seen in adults over 24.
Adults 65 and older actually showed a reduced risk.
Anyone starting this medicine should be closely monitored for worsening mood or new or worsening suicidal thoughts.
Families and caregivers should stay in regular contact with the prescriber.
Other warnings:
Serotonin syndrome: A potentially life-threatening condition that can occur when serotonin builds up to dangerous levels.
This can occur when taken alone.
It is more likely when taken with other serotonergic medications.

The initial dose is 150 mg orally per day in divided doses.

The reduction depends on therapeutic response.
This occurs after an adequate response has been reached.
If drowsiness develops, a major portion of the daily dose may be administered at bedtime.
If drowsiness develops, a reduction of dosage may be necessary.
-This drug should be taken shortly after a meal or light snack.

graph_edge.subject: Trazodone
graph_edge.object: 150 mg orally per day in divided doses
graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug is typically prescribed at the dose or dosing regimen specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Usual Adult Dose for Depression:
The initial dose is 150 mg orally per day in divided doses.
This dose may be increased by 50 mg orally per day every 3 to 4 days.
The maximum dose for inpatients is 600 mg/day.
The maximum dose for outpatients is 400 mg/day.
Patients should be screened for a personal or family history of bipolar disorder, mania, or hypomania prior to initiating treatment.
-Patients should be monitored for withdrawal symptoms when discontinuing therapy.
Dosage may be gradually reduced.
The reduction depends on therapeutic response.
This occurs after an adequate response has been reached.
If drowsiness develops, a major portion of the daily dose may be administered at bedtime.
If drowsiness develops, a reduction of dosage may be necessary.
-This drug should be taken shortly after a meal or light snack.
Use: Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD)

graph_edge.subject: amoxicillin
graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological or therapeutic drug class specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.

severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or

This is not a complete list of side effects.

Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Examples of cephalosporins include Omnicef, Cefzil, Ceftin, and Keflex.

Tell your doctor if you have liver disease.
Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease.
Tell your doctor if you have a bleeding or blood-clotting disorder.
Tell your doctor if you have mononucleosis (also called "mono").
Tell your doctor if you have any type of allergy.
Amoxicillin can make birth control pills less effective.

candidate_edges.subject: amoxicillin
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

graph_edge.subject: Tamsulosin
graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

They include needing to urinate often or urgently.

Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
The medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

candidate_edges.subject: Tamsulosin
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug should not be co-administered with the object drug.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
The medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, itching, rash, swelling of your face, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing.
Rarely, tamsulosin has been linked to severe skin reactions with blistering and peeling of the skin.
Stop taking tamsulosin and call your doctor at once if you have:
a lightheaded feeling, like you might pass out
a painful erection that will not go away and is not related to sexual activity
What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:
Common tamsulosin side effects may include:
headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision
Some side effects are more likely at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at the usual 0.4 mg starting dose.
In clinical studies, abnormal ejaculation was reported by about 8 in 100 men taking 0.4 mg.

graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, itching, rash, swelling of your face, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing.
Rarely, tamsulosin has been linked to severe skin reactions with blistering and peeling of the skin.
Stop taking tamsulosin and call your doctor at once if you have:
a lightheaded feeling, like you might pass out
a painful erection that will not go away and is not related to sexual activity
What are the common side effects of tamsulosin?
:
Common tamsulosin side effects may include:
headache
dizziness
runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, sinus congestion
flu-like symptoms or infection
weakness or lack of energy
back pain, chest pain
diarrhea, nausea
drowsiness or trouble sleeping
tooth problems
abnormal ejaculation, including a smaller amount of semen or no semen at all
reduced interest in sex
blurred vision
Some side effects are more likely at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at the usual 0.4 mg starting dose.
In clinical studies, abnormal ejaculation was reported by about 8 in 100 men taking 0.4 mg.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.
