graph_edge.evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.
3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
The relationship also explains some of its most important drug interactions.

Spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic.
Spironolactone is used for heart failure.
Spironolactone is used for high blood pressure.
Spironolactone is used for fluid build-up caused by liver or kidney disease.
Spironolactone is used for a hormone condition called primary hyperaldosteronism.
Spironolactone is sometimes prescribed off-label for women with acne or excessive facial hair growth (hirsutism).
Spironolactone works by blocking a hormone called aldosterone.
Aldosterone causes your body to pass more salt and water in your urine.
Aldosterone keeps potassium in.
This is why it is called potassium-sparing.
It is what makes spironolactone different from most other water pills.
Most other water pills flush potassium out.
Spironolactone blocks androgens such as testosterone from binding to the androgen receptor.
This mechanism explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include breast tenderness and breast growth.

The main long-term concerns with spironolactone are chemical rather than something you would feel.
Over time, it can push your potassium too high.
Over time, it can lower your sodium.
Over time, it can lower your magnesium.
Over time, it can lower your calcium.
Over time, it can raise your blood sugar.
Over time, it can raise your uric acid.
High uric acid occasionally brings on gout.
This is why you need regular blood tests for as long as you take it, not just at the start.
In animal studies, spironolactone given at high doses over long periods caused tumors in rats.
The tumors were mainly in hormone-producing glands and the liver.
No increase in tumors was seen at the lower doses tested.
These doses were still around five times the highest recommended human dose when adjusted for body size.
Whether this happens in people is not known.
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Is spironolactone a blood thinner?
:
No.
Spironolactone is not a blood thinner.
It does not affect blood clotting.
It is not used to prevent clots or strokes.
Warfarin, apixaban, or aspirin are used to prevent clots or strokes.
It is a diuretic that lowers blood pressure and reduces fluid build-up.
Spironolactone does interact with some blood thinners indirectly.
Heparin and low molecular weight heparin can raise potassium.
Taking them with spironolactone increases the risk of a high potassium level.
Can I stop taking spironolactone suddenly?
:
Spironolactone does not cause withdrawal symptoms.
Spironolactone does not need to be tapered the way a steroid does.
Even so, do not stop it without speaking to your doctor.
Stopping it can allow fluid to build up again.
Stopping it can allow your blood pressure to rise.
Stopping it can allow your heart failure to worsen.

Over time, it can lower your sodium.

The main long-term concerns with spironolactone are chemical rather than something you would feel.
Over time, it can push your potassium too high.
Over time, it can lower your sodium.
Over time, it can lower your magnesium.
Over time, it can lower your calcium.
Over time, it can raise your blood sugar.
Over time, it can raise your uric acid.

This is why you need regular blood tests for as long as you take it, not just at the start.
In animal studies, spironolactone given at high doses over long periods caused tumors in rats.
The tumors were mainly in hormone-producing glands and the liver.
No increase in tumors was seen at the lower doses tested.
These doses were still around five times the highest recommended human dose when adjusted for body size.
Whether this happens in people is not known.
This is not a complete list of side effects.
